case_title.quote: SIDDALING v. THE STATE, THROUGH KALAGI POLICE STATION

number_of_accused.quote: The appellant, accused-husband, has been convicted under Section 498-A I.P.C. and 306 I.P.C.
number_of_accused.reason: Only the appellant's liability is decided; father was acquitted by High Court.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: Marriage of the appellant-Siddaling was solemnized with the deceased-Kavitha

offence_category.correct_value: Other (abetment of suicide, s.306, with cruelty s.498-A)
offence_category.quote: convicted under Section 498-A I.P.C. and 306 I.P.C.
offence_category.reason: Cruelty is plausible but the more serious conviction is abetment of suicide.

statutory_provisions.quote: Sections 498-A and 304-B r/w 34 I.P.C. and Sections 306 r/w 34 I.P.C. and Sections 3, 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act
statutory_provisions.reason: Accurately lists charges and what remains.

weapon.reason: No weapon; suicide by drowning in well.

evidence_type.quote: PW-1... PW-10... PW-6... PW-22... Agreement dated 22nd June, 2002
evidence_type.reason: Oral and documentary evidence accurately described.

confession.quote: the appellant has admitted to be living with another woman
confession.reason: Admission in panchayat agreement relied upon.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: within four months of her marriage... also within three months of convening the panchayat

trial_court_outcome.correct_value: Convicted appellant and his father under ss.498-A, 304-B r/w 34, 306 r/w 34 IPC and Dowry Prohibition Act ss.3, 4, 6; sentence not stated
trial_court_outcome.quote: The trial court convicted the appellant-accused and also his father
trial_court_outcome.reason: Omits that father was also convicted; otherwise accurate.

high_court_outcome.quote: The High Court partly allowed the appeal and acquitted the appellant's father

offence_finally_established.quote: maintained the conviction of the appellant under Sections 498-A and 306 I.P.C.

imprisonment_type.quote: rigorous imprisonment for two years and five years respectively

imprisonment_years.correct_value: 5 (concurrent not stated; two years under 498-A and five years under 306)
imprisonment_years.quote: rigorous imprisonment for two years and five years respectively
imprisonment_years.reason: Five years for s.306; whether concurrent is not stated.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Remove 'the accused agreed ... to live with the victim' gender-neutral issues; avoid pronoun-free but mentions 'married to the accused' is fine; main problem: 'according to the prosecution' ok
neutral_facts.quote: The appellant was having illicit relationship with one woman
neutral_facts.reason: Largely accurate, but it describes the Panchayat agreement 'seen by victim' fine; no clear contradiction, though 'victim's house' fine.

physical_harm.quote: Kavitha committed suicide by jumping into a well of the village.

number_of_offences.quote: Sections 498-A and 304-B r/w 34 ... 306 r/w 34 ... Sections 3, 4 and 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act

financial_property_loss.reason: No loss; dowry demand only alleged.

motive.quote: would have definitely created the psychological imbalance to the deceased

key_evidence_accepted.quote: based upon the evidence and also Agreement dated 22nd June, 2002

witness_credibility.quote: have clearly in their statement stated that the appellant continued his relation
witness_credibility.reason: Court relied on witnesses without detailed analysis.

trial_duration.reason: Dates correct; trial date not given.

legal_representation.quote: Girish Ananthamurthy, Mrs. Vaijayanthi Girish, Advs. for the Appellant. Joseph Aristotle S., Ms. Anitha Shenoy, Advs. for the Respondent.

defence_argument.quote: there has to be a mens rea... praying for leniency in the quantum of sentence

legal_principle_applied.correct_value: Abetment involves a mental process of instigating or aiding; courts must assess facts of each case on whether cruelty induced suicide
legal_principle_applied.quote: abetment involves a mental process of instigating a person or in any manner aiding that person
legal_principle_applied.reason: Last clause 'negating s.306 defence' is garbled but substance largely right.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Randhir Singh v. State of Punjab, (2004) 13 SCC 129

sentencing_rationale.quote: showing any leniency would be a misplaced one

judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: within four months of her marriage... within three months of convening the panchayat
